1.name: Body
1.note: The cast pressure casing. The vessel connects below and the discharge leaves sideways.

2.name: Nozzle
2.note: The inlet and seat. Its throat is the flow diameter d0, and the disc closes on its rim.

3.name: Adjusting ring
3.note: Screws on the nozzle and sets the width of the gap round the disc, which tunes the pop and the blowdown.

4.name: Ring lock screw
4.note: Locks the adjusting ring so the setting cannot drift.

5.name: Disc
5.note: The sealing member. The vessel pressure over the seat area pushes it up against the spring; it lifts when that force passes the preload.

6.name: Disc holder
6.note: Carries the disc. Its skirt makes the huddling chamber: gas there acts on a larger area, so the valve pops and stays open.

7.name: Guide
7.note: Keeps the holder central as it lifts. At full lift the holder strikes it.

8.name: Spindle
8.note: Carries the spring force down onto the disc, and the lift up from the disc to the spring.

9.name: Split ring
9.note: Retains the spindle in the disc holder, so the disc follows the lift of the spindle.

10.name: Bonnet
10.note: The cast housing for the spring and spindle, bolted to the body.

11.name: Stud
11.note: Hold the bonnet down on the body against the pressure.

12.name: Hex nut
12.note: Tighten the bonnet on the studs.

13.name: Gasket
13.note: Seals the joint between the body and the bonnet.

14.name: Lower spring plate
14.note: Seats the bottom of the spring on the spindle.

15.name: Spring
15.note: Sets the pressure. Its preload over the seat area is the opening pressure, and its stiffness sets how the force rises with lift.

16.name: Upper spring plate
16.note: Seats the top of the spring and takes the load from the adjusting screw.

17.name: Adjusting screw
17.note: Compresses the spring. Turning it changes the preload, and so the set pressure.

18.name: Lock nut
18.note: Locks the adjusting screw so that the set pressure holds.

19.name: Cap
19.note: Covers the adjusting screw and the spindle top, to keep the setting from being altered.

20.name: Lifting lever
20.note: Lets the valve be lifted by hand to check it moves freely.

21.name: Lever pin
21.note: The pivot of the lifting lever.

22.name: Lifting nut
22.note: On the spindle top, where the lever pulls upward to lift the disc.

23.name: Drain plug
23.note: Closes the drain hole in the outlet side of the body, so liquid that collects there can be drained.
